newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: ERM no guarantee of currency stability - Asbrink.
newsitem.headline: ERM no guarantee of currency stability - Asbrink.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Monday that membership of the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) not in itself a good indicator of currency stability.
Asbrink said that Finland's decision on Saturday to join the ERM had not changed his country's position and he reitereated that Swedish membership was not a current issue.

He said the widening of ERM fluctuation bands to 15 percent in 1993, from the original 2.25 percent band agreed within the Maastricht Treaty negotiations of 1991, had robbed the criterion had of much of its original significance.
"This (the ERM) is no longer a good measure of currency stability," he told reporters on the margins of a meeting of EU economic and finace ministers.

But he acknowledged that there were different views on the issue among EU member states and that the EU leaders would take a final decision until early 1998 on which countries qualify to join the single currency.
Asbrink said that until then, there would be some uncertainty about the interpretation of all five convergence criteria required for countries to qualify.
"We know very well what we are doing...I'm not worried because of this," he said, noting that most countries had difficulties meeting one or two of these criteria.
